ruleset.name: Best Practices
ruleset.description: Rules which enforce generally accepted best practices.

rule.name: FunctionNameTooShort
rule.message: Function names should have non-cryptic and clear names.
rule.description: Function names should be easy to understand and describe the intention. Makes developers happy.
rule.example:
fun cl() {} // violation, no unavailable attribute added to the function declaration
fun calculateLayout() // no violation

rule.name: LocalVariableShadowsParameter
rule.message: Local variable ''{0}'' shadows a parameter of the enclosing function.
rule.description: A local variable declaration uses the same name as a parameter of the enclosing function. This shadows the parameter and may lead to confusion about which value is used.

rule.name: LooseCoupling
rule.message: Avoid using implementation types (e.g. ArrayList, HashMap); use the corresponding interface (e.g. List, Map) instead
rule.description:
Excessive coupling to implementation types (e.g., `HashMap`) limits your ability to use alternate implementations in the future as requirements change. Whenever available, declare properties, parameters, and return types using a more general type (e.g., `Map`).
Note that Kotlin's `List` / `Map` / `Set` are read-only interfaces, distinct from the mutable `MutableList` / `MutableMap` / `MutableSet`. Prefer the read-only interface by default; only fall back to the `Mutable*` variant when the value genuinely needs to be mutated after declaration (e.g. `put`, `add`, `remove`).
This rule reports uses of concrete collection/map types. It currently checks a fixed list of common JDK implementation types (e.g. `ArrayList`, `HashMap`, `TreeSet`); unlike the Java version of this rule, it does not yet generically detect *any* concrete `Collection`/`Map` implementation, since that would require a dedicated type-introspection XPath function (see https://github.com/pmd/pmd/issues/7091). User-defined types that should be treated the same as interfaces can be configured with the property `allowedTypes`. Local variables are not reported, since their type is not part of the API surface.

property.name: allowedTypes
property.description: Exceptions to the rule: types that should be treated the same as interfaces even though they are concrete implementation types.

property.name: xpath
property.value: ( //PropertyDeclaration[not(ancestor::FunctionBody or ancestor::AnonymousInitializer or ancestor::SecondaryConstructor)] | //ClassParameter | //FunctionValueParameter[ancestor::FunctionDeclaration] | //FunctionDeclaration ) [not(pmd-kotlin:modifiers() = 'override')] [ pmd-kotlin:typeIs('java.util.ArrayList') or pmd-kotlin:typeIs('java.util.LinkedList') or pmd-kotlin:typeIs('java.util.Vector') or pmd-kotlin:typeIs('java.util.Stack') or pmd-kotlin:typeIs('java.util.HashMap') or pmd-kotlin:typeIs('java.util.Hashtable') or pmd-kotlin:typeIs('java.util.LinkedHashMap') or pmd-kotlin:typeIs('java.util.TreeMap') or pmd-kotlin:typeIs('java.util.HashSet') or pmd-kotlin:typeIs('java.util.LinkedHashSet') or pmd-kotlin:typeIs('java.util.TreeSet') ] [not(some $t in $allowedTypes satisfies pmd-kotlin:typeIsExactly($t))]
